steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Place potatoes in skillet, cover, and simmer. Turn occasionally until potatoes are almost tender and a little browned, about 10 minutes.
Stir in sausage, onions, and peppers. Cover and cook for about 5 minutes or until onions and peppers are desired tenderness.

raw_recipe.headline: S.O.P.P.
raw_recipe.description: This S.O.P.P (sausage, onions, potatoes, and peppers) skillet dish tastes delicious and is easy to whip up for your family any day of the week!
raw_recipe.name: S.O.P.P.

recipeInstructions.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Place potatoes in skillet, cover, and simmer. Turn occasionally until potatoes are almost tender and a little browned, about 10 minutes.
Stir in sausage, onions, and peppers. Cover and cook for about 5 minutes or until onions and peppers are desired tenderness.

review.reviewBody: I have made a similar recipe like this for years, but instead of smoked sausage, you MUST try this with Italian sausage (hot or mild). I start this off by heating a little olive oil in a skillet and start cooking my potatoes. After the potatoes have a good start, I add the hot sausage, cut into cubes as well and cook that. This gives the potatoes a WONDERFUL flavor. I then add sliced red and green peppers and sliced onions. I put a lid on it and let it cook so that the potatoes get soft. YUMMY! This is great on a buffet for a party. I haven't made this for a while, but writing this review has made me hungry for it, and now I know what tomorrow's dinner will be!

A small hint about cooking potatoes: If you like your potatoes a little more firm, salt when you start them to cook. If you like them softer, salt when they are about half way done or when finished cooking. Has always worked for me :-)

Love this! I cooked potatoes in microwave to soften first. sprinkled with garlic pepper, added minced garlic and used 1 kielbasa and 1 cup of smokies. Didn't have peppers but added green beans. at the end I put 2 tblsp. garlic butter. Delicious, easy and can be made any way you want too.

This has been a staple in my home for years. If you cook the potatoes like the recipe states, it takes longer than 10 min. and uses more oil than necessary, which is why I gave 4 instead of 5 stars. I have always microwaved the potatoes just until tender. Use a little olive oil and saute the onions and peppers with a clove of garlic until tender. Then add the smoked sausage and potatoes. I use red potatoes (which are smaller) and only 1 pound of sausage. Then salt and pepper to taste. Quick and tasty meal.

I grew up eating this and have also made it for years. Instead of preparing in a skillet I use a baking pan and cook it in the oven. I drizzle olive oil on the bottom of the pan, use italian sausage instead of smoked and add whatever type of peppers I have on hand. I also season w/Adobo. Bake 375 for 45-60 minutes. A great meal in one and only use one pan!

I say use the following ratio instead: 16 oz fully cooked smoked sausage, 2 medium size onions, 3 large potatoes, and 3 green bell peppers. To use one pot for this is a bit ambitious. You can, but by the time you stir everything around enough for the onions and bell peppers to cook up nicely you've somewhat mangled the potato cubes. I suggest cooking up the potatoes in a large pot and at the same time basically stir frying your sausage, onion, and bell peppers. Also, if one gets finished before the other you can turn it to low that way and avoid mushy veggies. Honestly I put just a light sprinkling of salt on the potatoes twice, and the recipe tastes great without any additional seasoning!

My version makes a little less than this but includes 5 red potatoes cubed with skin on, 1 lb smoked sausage sliced, 1 onion cubed, 1 red bell pepper cubed, 1/2 cup water give or take and one package of Lipton Onion Soup mix. Brown sauage a bit, throw in onions, pepper, water, and onion soup mix, cover and cook until potatoes are tender. The pototes release water as they cook so don't add too much water. When done, let set for 5 minutes for broth to thicken. Yummy!!!

Oh....my....word!! We loved this, with only a few changes. I only made half for my husband and I, and it was still plenty. First I used smoked turkey sausage to cut the fat. I roasted baby red potatoes but seasoned them with garlic powder, onion powder, salt, pepper and some basil. While they were roasting I cut up everything else. I kept that the same but I added 2 cloves of garlic. After that was fried I added the potatoes. It was one of the best dinners we had in a while! It quickly became a favorite....i took leftovers for lunch today and it was still just as wonderful. Thanks sooo much :-)

Super Yummy!! We all loved it. I didn't have green bell peppers, so I used yellow and orange bell peppers. I did add some veggies for additional color like green beans, wax beans, a little bit of red pepper and a carrot. I cooked the potatoes separately from the sausage, like a user suggested, and I added salt to the potatoes at the beginning like another user suggested for more firm potatoes. It did work! my potatoes were not mushy, I added a little bit of black pepper too. I tried the meal before I added the extra veggies and it was already delicious, so for the flavor it didn't need anything else, I just wanted more color, and to be able to feed more veggies to the kids.

I've been making this recipe for years now, both as written and with various modifications. It’s always our first dinner meal to make on our Northwoods WI or MI cabin trips. It’s easy to make, quite tasty, and perfect for a quick meal on a cold night. I always use 1 red and 1 yellow bell pepper (we don't care for green peppers). I find that adding salt to the potatoes and stirring them around a bit seems to result in less mushy potatoes. Add the remaining ingredients when potatoes are just starting to get tender. The sausage will take longer than 5 minutes to cook through. Just stir the potatoes, onions, peppers, and sausage every now and then. The potatoes will finish cooking by the time the other ingredients are done. I will note that I have never gotten the potatoes to brown as shown in the picture, but perhaps that can be accomplished if you cook the potatoes separate from the sausage, onions, and peppers and mix together at the end, resulting in potatoes not becoming mush. VARIATIONS: Try seasoning potatoes with salt, black pepper, garlic powder (or even 1 clove garlic, minced), onion powder, paprika, and herbs such as basil, parsley, oregano, thyme etc. I’ve also lightly salted/seasoned each layer of ingredients (i.e. potatoes first, then a little more seasoning to onions, peppers, and sausage). Be careful not to over salt as the sausage already has a higher salt content.

I make this same recipe but I do it in the oven! Cut the potatoes bite sized, as well as the sausage and add the peppers and onions. Put in casserole dish, sprinkle with black pepper and paprika and cover. Cook at 350 degrees for 45 minutes, uncover and bake an additional 15 minutes. Delish!

Total winner. It was easy to make even though i did change the recipe a little. I did add 4 cloves of fresh garlic minced which gives you a good indication when to add the potatoes. i did decrease the amount of onions but added more sausage. Cook times were a little longer than expected but still ended up being a great meal.
Our family always comes back to this recipe, and we all love it! It's easy to make and budget friendly.
Good, but needed a little kick. Add Monterey Seasoning to bring out flavors.
Used red bell peppers instead of green. Quick, easy and everyone loved it.
This was a hit at my house!

I've used it a lot in different ways, for example, adding scrambled eggs, sausage, browned crumbled beef, kielbasa, fresh caught butter fried pike and perch. I've even had it with shredded lamb, rabbit and, although I wasn't the one that made it this way, on the border. Sometimes, I'll add Mexican, or Cajon seasoning stuffing it into pita pockets or soft taco shells, and freeze them for future uses Just a great all around recipe.
Very good. Simple, quick recipe. I quartered small klondike gourmet potatoes and seasoned them w cajun seasoning. It all came together so well.
Great recipe! This is also great to serve for breakfast by topping with eggs cooked to your liking and hollandaise sauce.
